conclusion: No model is involved anywhere in this round. Over 5,564 coval_full criteria rated by at least 4 people (92,463 ratings from 1,158 raters), the share of rating variance that is BETWEEN criteria rather than between raters of the same criterion is ICC(1) = 0.2698 [0.2586, 0.2809]. The floor that makes that number mean anything is a rater-style null -- each person's own ratings reassigned across the criteria they rated, preserving their scale usage and extremeness exactly -- which gives 0.0008 (sd 0.0012). Excess over the floor: +0.2689 against a pre-registered margin of 0.1. The estimator recovers planted ICCs of 0.0, 0.3 and 0.7 as 0.0002, 0.2975, 0.6996, and permuting within a criterion returns the observed value to 0.00e+00. On the scale itself, 16.5% of all ratings are exactly +10 or -10 and 20 of the 21 available values are used at all. WORLD: W-WEAK-STANDARD. Something shared exists and is swamped by disagreement: an aggregate summarises a minority of the variance in what people said mattered, and must be stated as such rather than as the panel's view.
